title: Why San Diego's Heat Pump Rebate Looks Different (2026)
desc: San Diego has no open utility heat pump rebate, but San Diego Community Power pays $250 to $500 per kWh for batteries. Who does what, and what SDG&E lists in 2026.
h1: Why San Diego's Heat Pump Rebate Looks Different
lead: An earlier version of this post blamed a milder climate and quoted heating degree days we could not source. The better explanation is structural: two organizations serve a San Diego home, and the money they offer points at batteries and smart devices, not heat pumps. Read from their own pages on October 2, 2026.
sections: San Diego Community Power (SDCP) supplies the electricity to the City of San Diego, Chula Vista and several other cities, and runs the rebates. SDG&E delivers the power and runs its own programs. Escondido is not an SDCP member, so its customers deal with SDG&E alone. Neither lists an open cash rebate for a heat pump or heat pump water heater on the pages we could read.

SDG&E's rebates page lists retail coupons: $75 for an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat, $40 for an Amazon model, $500 for a heat pump water heater replacing an electric one, and $15 for a room air conditioner. The same page says the retail offerings have ended, so we do not count them (SDG&E rebates). Its home electrification page notes a billing change in October 2025 that lowered the delivery price per kWh by about 10%.

SDCP's Solar Battery Savings program pays $250 to $500 per kWh of battery depending on whether the system is new, and on the customer type, plus $0.10 per kWh for discharging in the weekday evening window. Smart Energy Rewards pays $50 for each approved thermostat or heat pump water heater (up to three of each) plus yearly payments, and EV Flex Connect pays $50 plus $5 a month. Income-qualified households in identified communities can get no-cost upgrades, including heat pumps, through the Equitable Building Decarbonization program. See San Diego rebates.
What this means for your choice

If you are weighing a heat pump against solar and a battery, San Diego's published incentives favor the battery side. For a heat pump, check the no-cost program first if your income may qualify, and otherwise budget without a rebate and get three bids. San Diego's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 8.8°C, so a heat pump's cooling benefit in summer is part of the case.
faq: Does SDG&E have a heat pump rebate?
Not that we found. Its rebates page lists retail coupons and says the retail offerings have ended.
Does San Diego Community Power pay for batteries?
Yes, $250 to $500 per kWh of battery, plus $0.10 per kWh for evening discharge.
SDG&E. Escondido is not an SDCP member.
